records.text: After rewatching the testimony, Owens corrected her inference that Lance Twiggs and Amber Robinson had been identified on the rifle: among the three additional people she had named, only Matt Robinson was explicitly identified; she said Twiggs's presence remained unknown.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Never officially said that Lance (Lance Twiggs)'s DNA was on the rifle. And so they just kind of played that and it was weird and I allowed it. I totally allowed the silence because A, never get in the way of your opponent when they're making a mistake.
I think I wrongly extrapolated that they meant all three of them were on the prints when the only person they officially named was Matt Robinson.

I had to rewatch the testimony again. It's like nine hours a day. It got very scientific when they were speaking about this. And I think I wrongly extrapolated that they meant all three of them were on the print when the only person they officially named was Matt Robinson. ... So we don't know yet if Lance Twiggs has his DNA on the print, DNA on the gun officially just yet.

verification.notes: The source episode records Owens making the correction. Day 5 testimony supports the substance: Matthew Robinson was associated with the rifle bolt, while Lance Twiggs was associated with the Dremel rather than the rifle; Amber Robinson was not identified as a rifle contributor in the reviewed testimony.

records.text: Owens said no proof had been produced that Tyler Robinson's parents turned him in or believed he was guilty.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And this early narrative that Tyler Robinson's parents turned him in, that Tyler Robinson's parents thought he was guilty, they have not produced any proof of that.

verification.notes: The source appearance was reviewed at 00:30:18. The official charging information filed September 16, 2025 directly records that Robinson's mother thought the released image looked like her son, his father agreed, both parents discussed surrender with him, and they convinced him to speak with a retired-deputy family friend who helped arrange the surrender. That is public evidentiary material directly contradicting the categorical claim that no proof had been produced. These are allegations in a charging document, not a finding of Robinson's guilt.
